meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 이제 다 됐어, 낙서 지우는 데 좀 시간이 걸렸어. 주차장 도착하면 다시 전화할게.
examples.trans: It is all finished now—scrubbing off the graffiti took a while. I will call again once I reach the parking lot.
Let us do that (it took) right away.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.
Did you hear about this muscle?
I was busy today because of muscle.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

examples.text: 이제 다 됐어, 낙서 지우는 데 좀 시간이 걸렸어. 주차장 도착하면 다시 전화할게.
examples.trans: It is all finished now—scrubbing off the graffiti took a while. I will call again once I reach the parking lot.
This point about graffiti, scribbling is really important.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: repeating an action or returning to a previous state

examples.trans: Please say that one more time.
I'll come back in a moment.
Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

examples.text: 내가 당분간 너 술 먹지 말라 그랬지, 입 조심해야 된다고!
examples.trans: I told you not to drink for the time being because you have to watch your mouth!
Here the word for 'for the time being' is key.

meanings.note: Bound noun referring to a location.

examples.trans: I have no place to go.
I have no place to go. (2)

examples.text: 조금만 더 가면 금방 도착할 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: If we go just a little farther, we should arrive soon.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 도착하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (will arrive).

examples.text: 어떤 회사는 뮤직뱅크에서 1등을 해도 백설기 한 쪽 돌리고 마는데.
examples.trans: Some agencies win first place on Music Bank and hand out nothing more than a plain slice of white rice cake.
This expression comes from 'hand around and'.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

examples.text: 아 미치겠네, 이거 봐 손 떨리는 거!
examples.trans: Oh man, look at my hands shaking right here!

examples.text: 저희 어머님은 가수 전영록 씨 노래를 들으면 아직도 옛날 연애하던 좋았던 시절이 생각나서 가슴이 떨리고 좋으시답니다.
examples.trans: Whenever my mother hears singer Jeon Young-rok's songs, her heart still flutters happily remembering the sweet days when she was young and in love.

examples.text: 일단 그거 떼시고요, 당분간 조심하셔야 될 것 같습니다. 어디서 누가 튀어나와서 해코지할지 모르니까.
examples.trans: Take that card off first, and please stay careful for a while—you never know who might jump out to harm you.

examples.text: 일단 그거 떼시고요, 당분간 조심하셔야 될 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: Take that card down first, and please stay cautious for the time being.
See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?
Have you lost your mind? You are driving me crazy—no way!
This expression comes from 'driving me nuts'.
Is that the Viking ship ride over there? Wait—what is happening right now?
This point about is it the Viking ship is really important.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 근데 백승찬, 나 너한테 약간 부끄러우려고 그런다.
examples.trans: Still, Baek Seung-chan, I am starting to feel a little embarrassed in front of you.
This expression comes from 'about to feel embarrassed'.

examples.text: 전화번호 어떻게 알았을까요? 아, 차 창문 앞에 붙여놓은 전화번호!
examples.trans: How could they have found your phone number? Ah—the contact number posted inside your windshield!

examples.text: 어떻게 알았을까요? 창문 앞에 붙여놓은 전화번호!
examples.trans: How could they have known? The phone number stuck inside the windshield!

examples.text: 아 진짜 나를 팽이처럼 빙빙 돌리고!
examples.trans: Ugh, that ride spun me round and round like a top!
I thought it over again (round and round).
Wash your hands.
Raise your right hand.

meanings.note: Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.
Go forward.
Do well in the future.
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?
Hey, Baek Seung-chan, are you just getting back now?
Here the word for 'hey' is key.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

examples.text: 너 오버 좀 하지 마! 누가 보면 내가 진짜 대단한 공갈 협박이라도 당하고 있는 줄 알겠어.
examples.trans: Stop overreacting! Anyone watching would think I am facing some massive blackmail threat.
Baek Seung-chan is such a worrywart.
Why are you running?
Why were you late today?
How much is this?
Please look at this.

meanings.note: Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
The performance is starting very soon now.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

examples.text: 일 호선이 가장 오래된 지하철 노선이에요.
examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.

meanings.en: first of all, for starters, for the time being
meanings.note: marks an immediate first step before dealing with anything else

examples.trans: Let's sit down and talk first.
Let's wait until today for now.

examples.text: 저거 백승찬 아니야? 왜 우리 집에 자고 있냐고.
examples.trans: Isn't that Baek Seung-chan? Why is he sleeping in our house?
The topic of that person/thing over there came up during this shoot.
What is your phone number?
I changed my phone number.

meanings.note: The person called is marked with 에게 or 한테 (e.g., 친구한테 전화하다).

examples.trans: Please call me when you arrive.
I'll call right now.

meanings.note: Used to warn or advise caution.

examples.trans: Please be careful.
Please be careful. (2)
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

examples.text: 내가 VIP 동선을 주차장에서 지정석 착석까지 완벽하게 다 확인했다!
examples.trans: I double-checked the entire VIP route flawlessly from the parking lot right to their assigned seats!
Here the word for 'from the parking lot' is key.
I want to they meant erase right now.
How about trying to they meant erase together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

examples.text: 여긴 창문도 없다고, 감방에 독방 같잖아?
examples.trans: There are no windows in here—does it not look just like solitary confinement?
Here the word for 'even windows' is key.

examples.text: 아 진짜 나를 팽이처럼 빙빙 돌리고!
examples.trans: Ugh, that ride spun me round and round like a top!
This point about like a spinning top is really important.
